overall: The AG found the Board violated the OML by discussing an unrelated cruiser-lettering invoice in a Purpose 2 executive session, but found the later open-session vote on the invoice effectively cured it; the non-OML conduct claims were declined.

allegations.summary: During a Nov. 22, 2010 executive session, the vice chair allegedly raised an unrelated invoice (police cruiser lettering), beyond the stated Purpose 2 negotiation session.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board considered a topic that was not appropriate for consideration under the specific purpose cited when it entered executive session during its November 22, 2010 meeting.

allegations.summary: The complaint also alleged the vice chair made false statements and conducted public business despite a conflict of interest, which are not Open Meeting Law claims.
allegations.key_passage: Because these are complaints that do not allege a violation of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25, we decline to review them, and have advised the complainant that these matters are more appropriate for other agencies
